qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture eighteen. Neuromorphic computing. How a chip shaped like a brain spends energy only when something happens.
Priya's camera, Hoglet, watches her garden for hedgehogs all night. Its battery dies by Tuesday.
Hoglet watches the garden for hedgehogs all night.
Inside is an ordinary von Neumann computer: a processor here, a separate memory there.
Inside: a von Neumann computer, processor and memory apart.
A program tells it what to do, one step at a time, in binary.
A program runs step by step, in binary.
So data shuttles back and forth all night, and every trip costs time and energy.
Data shuttles back and forth, and every trip costs energy.
A neuromorphic computer works like a brain. Each synapse both stores data and computes.
In a neuromorphic computer, synapses store data and process it.
There is no program as such. Who connects to whom, and how strongly, sets what it does.
No program as such: the synapse structure sets what it does.
Its inputs are spikes. When they arrive, and how big they are, carry the information.
Inputs are spikes; their timing and magnitude carry information.
The word began in the nineteen eighties. Today it covers many brain-inspired techniques.
The term began in the 1980s; today it covers many brain-inspired ideas.
First, it is parallel. All its neurons work at once, each doing something simple.
Parallel: all neurons work at once, each doing something simple.
Second, memory and processing sit together, so there are no trips. It is faster and uses less energy.
Processing and memory together: faster and less energy.
Third, it scales. For a bigger network, add more chips and connect them.
Scalable: need a bigger network? Add more chips.
The fourth superpower is the one Hoglet needs most. It is event driven.
And the fourth: it is event driven.
On this quiet night, something happens at only four of twenty-four moments.
A quiet night: a spike at only 4 of 24 moments.
A clocked chip works all twenty-four times. The event-driven chip works just four times.
The clocked chip works 24 times; the event-driven chip 4.
On a busier night, eleven moments bring a spike, so it works eleven times.
A busier garden: 11 spikes, 11 bursts of work.
With no spikes at all, it does no work. It computes only when a spike arrives.
No spikes, no work: it computes only when a spike arrives.
Problems shaped like networks fit a spiking chip. Graph algorithms route a message from A through B and D to E.
Graph algorithms: routing messages through a network.
Optimisation fits too, from constraint satisfaction and QUBO to optimal control.
Optimisation: constraint satisfaction, QUBO, optimal control.
Random walkers hop between neurons that stand for states, like a hedgehog roaming flower beds.
Random walkers hop between neurons that stand for states.
And signal processing, such as steering vehicles or detecting seizures.
Signal processing: steering vehicles, detecting seizures.
SpiNNaker has eighteen ARM cores per chip. One runs the system; the rest each model a group of neurons.
SpiNNaker: 18 ARM cores per chip, built for exploring.
One chip runs about sixteen thousand neurons in real time, on one watt.
About 16,000 neurons in real time on 1 W per chip.
SpiNNaker two, from twenty nineteen, is ten times bigger.
SpiNNaker 2, in 2019, is ten times bigger.
IBM's TrueNorth holds a million neurons per chip, set up in a language called Corelet.
IBM TrueNorth: 1 million neurons per chip, set up in Corelet.
NorthPole, from twenty twenty-three, aims to be easy to use, quick, and efficient for AI.
NorthPole, 2023: easier, faster, efficient AI.
Deep learning still gives better results. Neuromorphic chips win on energy, against edge GPUs.
Deep learning still wins on results; neuromorphic wins on energy.
There are few machines and simulators, and training takes a long time.
Little hardware and software to use, and long training times.
Deep learning had shared races such as ImageNet. Neuromorphic computing has no benchmark that uses timing.
No benchmark suite that tests the time aspect.
And networks are wired by hand, neuron by neuron, which is error prone.
Networks are wired neuron by neuron, which is error prone.
A frame camera sends every pixel, every moment. Here that is seventy-two pixels each time.
A frame camera sends all 72 pixels, every moment.
An event camera's pixel spikes only when its brightness changes. A walking hedgehog costs two pixels a moment.
An event camera's pixels spike only when brightness changes: 2.
When the hedgehog sits still, nothing changes, so nothing is sent.
Hedgehog sits still: the event camera sends nothing.
Sensor fusion uses the events to wake the frame camera for a proper photo.
Sensor fusion: wake the frame camera when events appear.
A GA or PSO could tune Hoglet. Both are parallel, but energy hungry on ordinary hardware.
GAs and PSO are parallel but energy hungry on normal hardware.
Neuromorphic units evolve candidates on their own clocks, while a manager keeps the search on track.
Neuromorphic heuristic units evolve candidates asynchronously.
With no spike, unit one steps towards the best: from two point eight to five point two, then six point three.
No spike: a heuristic step, towards the best so far.
A spike makes it jump, to one point three.
A spike: the neuron's own dynamics make a jump.
Promising, but still highly experimental.
Promising, but still highly experimental.
Synapses store data and compute, so there are no trips to memory.
It is event driven: it works only when a spike arrives.
It saves energy, but it is still experimental.
